output.brief: The rise in cancellations is mainly caused by the Quillbook accounting connector, not the price rise. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March, and the connector has since silently dropped or duplicated invoices: 58,300 across 1,212 accounts. 34% of those accounts have cancelled, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no failure. Churn in the Quillbook-connected accounts tripled to about 6%, and it is the same for price-locked Founders accounts and repriced accounts. Accounts with no connector, who are 76% of the base and fully exposed to the price rise, are flat at about 1.9%, including in the largest seat band. The earlier "bigger increase, more churn" pattern is because Quillbook users have more seats. The Tallymarsh change is tiny and within normal variation. I'm fairly confident, though the data is observational. Next: make the Quillbook v3 fix a scheduled top priority (3–4 weeks), and contact all affected accounts, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices. Make the connector's WARN-level failures visible on the health panel. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on, since it protects customers' books. Don't roll back the price, and hold off on the Tallymarsh rebuild. Instead, review the Tallymarsh log first.
